record.prompt: Please run scripts/cost.sh on data/orders-2026-10.tsv and tell me the total shipping cost for October. Don't edit the script or data/zone-rates.tsv.
record.final_answer:
Total shipping cost for October: **58.01**

But you should know: as shipped, the script fails on your data. `sh scripts/cost.sh data/orders-2026-10.tsv` exits 1 with:

    cost.sh: no rate for zone "north" (order A-1001)

Cause: `data/zone-rates.tsv` has Windows CRLF line endings (the orders file is LF). awk's `$3` therefore holds `north\r`, not `north`, so every zone lookup misses. The rate card being a spreadsheet export makes that likely to recur.

Since you asked me not to edit either file, I left both untouched (`git status` is clean) and fed the script a CR-stripped copy of the rate card in scratch:

    sed 's/\r$//' data/zone-rates.tsv > /tmp/hermes/cache/scratch/zone-rates.lf.tsv
    sh scripts/cost.sh data/orders-2026-10.tsv /tmp/hermes/cache/scratch/zone-rates.lf.tsv

    A-1001  north   6.94
    A-1002  south   6.28
    A-1003  island  15.25
    A-1004  north   15.10
    A-1005  south   9.03
    A-1006  north   5.41
    total           58.01

I cross-checked the total independently (sum of per-order costs, and a from-scratch recomputation from the rate card): 58.01 both ways.

The permanent fix is a one-character change in the script — strip `\r` on input, e.g. `-F'[\t\r]'` in the awk invocation, or `$3 = $3` after `sub(/\r$/,"")`. Say the word and I'll apply it.
